p|oficios|Forter: Fraud prevention for online shops: examines the device and the session when you are about to pay.
p|oficios|GUARDIANA: This program and its site: activating the license, buying, the guides.
p|oficios|Ogury: Advertising in mobile apps and sites.
p|oficios|Pubstack: Measures how a site’s ads perform.
p|oficios|Minute Media: Sports publisher and its ad auction.
p|oficios|Viously: Videos and video ads on news sites.
p|oficios|Optidigital: Runs and auctions the ads of media sites.
p|oficios|OpenWeb: Comments and community on news sites, with its advertising.
p|oficios|TradingView: Charts and market data for stocks, currencies and crypto.
p|oficios|Dodo Payments: Payment gateway: charges, issues the invoice and pays each country’s taxes.
p|oficios|beehiiv: Email newsletters: sends them and measures who opens them.
p|oficios|Rust Foundation: The package registry of the Rust language (crates.io).
p|oficios|Y Combinator: Startup accelerator; also the Hacker News forum.
p|oficios|Product Hunt: A showcase for new tech products.
p|oficios|hCaptcha: Captcha: checks you are not a robot before a form.
p|oficios|Yandex: Search engine and internet services; also advertising and web analytics (Metrica).
p|oficios|HubSpot: Marketing and sales: its code on a site follows visits and forms.
p|oficios|Help Scout: Customer support: a site’s help chat and support email.
p|oficios|iubenda: A site’s cookie banner and legal pages.
p|oficios|RudderStack: Collects usage events from a site or app and passes them on to its analytics and advertising tools.
p|oficios|Insider: Personalization and marketing: decides what an online shop shows you from how you browse.
p|oficios|Stape: Routes a site’s analytics and advertising through a server of the site’s own.
p|oficios|Seedtag: Advertising on news sites, chosen from the page’s content.
p|oficios|GfK: Audience measurement: counts who sees which site or video, for market research.
p|oficios|Didomi: The cookie window: collects and stores your consent answer for the site you are visiting.
p|oficios|Verve Group: Video and mobile advertising: auctions the ad slot you are about to see.
p|oficios|RTB House: Retargeting: shows you again what you looked at on another site.
p|oficios|FreeWheel: Television and video advertising, a Comcast company. “user-sync” is matching your identifier between companies.
p|oficios|OneTag: Ad auction: connects whoever sells the slot with whoever buys it.
p|oficios|Marfeel: Analytics and advertising for news sites: measures how you read and monetizes the page.
p|oficios|secure.avastdns.com: The antivirus’s own DNS: it resolves names by itself, and while it does GUARDIANA cannot see this computer’s.
p|oficios|AppsFlyer: Ad attribution: ties this device to the campaign that brought it.
p|oficios|Adjust: Ad attribution: which ad each install came from.
p|oficios|Branch: Links and attribution: ties a click to the install it caused.
p|oficios|Mixpanel: Product analytics: receives events like screen viewed, click or purchase.
p|oficios|Amplitude: Product analytics: measures what people do inside the app.
p|oficios|PostHog: Product analytics; in some setups it also records the session.
p|oficios|Segment: Data pipeline: routes one app’s events to other companies.
p|oficios|Customer.io: Automated emails and messages based on what you do in the app.
p|oficios|Braze: Messages and notifications based on each user’s behavior.
p|oficios|Intercom: Support chat: usually ties this device to a customer record.
p|oficios|Sentry: Error reports: they carry device model, version and some context.
p|oficios|Datadog: Technical monitoring: logs and performance of the app itself.
p|oficios|HUMAN Security: Anti-bot check: decides whether you are a person before letting you through.
p|oficios|Temu: Shop. Its own tracking names measure what you do inside.
p|oficios|Criteo: Advertising that follows you with what you looked at before.
p|oficios|Outbrain: Recommended advertising at the end of articles.
p|oficios|Taboola: Recommended advertising at the end of articles.
p|oficios|LiveRamp: Identity: turns a signed-in person into an identifier of its own (RampID) used to recognize you across different sites.
p|oficios|app-measurement.com: Firebase (Google) measurement: the heartbeat every few minutes keeps going with the app closed.
p|oficios|google-analytics.com: Google’s web measurement: counts visits and journeys.
p|oficios|googletagmanager.com: Tag loader: decides which measurement scripts enter the page.
p|oficios|doubleclick.net: Google advertising: auction and delivery of ads.
p|oficios|graph.facebook.com: Meta’s interface used by apps: it also measures installs and events.
p|oficios|Contentsquare: Records how you move around a site: clicks and scrolling (it is the company behind Hotjar).
p|panel|vp_intro: What each program on this computer does on the network, seen from outside: which companies it talks to, how much it uploads and downloads, what goes to addresses with no name in sight, and whether it sent a lot somewhere right after opening your files. Without opening anything: GUARDIANA counts, it does not decrypt.
p|panel|vp_no_disponible: Only Windows says which program sends and receives each packet. On this system GUARDIANA still sees the names asked for, but not the detail per program.
p|panel|vp_sin_dns_que: To addresses GUARDIANA saw no name asked for: a fixed address, the program's own resolver, or QUIC to an address learned elsewhere.
p|panel|vp_reenviado_que: What Windows says was sent again because the line lost it. Kept apart: it is not added to what was uploaded.
p|panel|vp_cadena_filas: {n} hours per program and company, each with the hash of the one before.
p|panel|vp_cadena_rota: The chained summary does not add up: some hour was changed after it was written.
p|panel|vp_cadena_vacia: The chained summary starts being written when the first full hour closes.
p|panel|vp_archivos_que: If you turn it on, GUARDIANA notes which files in your folders (Documents, Desktop, Downloads, Pictures) each program opens, by name only, and tells you when shortly after that program sends several megabytes to one company. It is a coincidence in time, not proof of what travelled: GUARDIANA does not see the content. The names stay on this computer for 24 hours and go in no export.
p|panel|vp_archivos_apagar: Turn off and delete the names
p|panel|vp_archivos_encendido: On: the names of the files opened in your folders are watched.
p|panel|vp_archivos_confirma_apagar: Turn off and delete the saved file names now?
p|panel|vp_frase_leyo: Possible transfer: {programa} read {n} files{archivos} and sent {mb} to {empresa}{pais} in {min} min
p|panel|vp_frase_leyo_1: Possible transfer: {programa} read 1 file{archivos} and sent {mb} to {empresa}{pais} in {min} min
p|panel|vp_frase_abrio: Possible transfer: {programa} opened {n} files{archivos} and sent {mb} to {empresa}{pais} in {min} min
p|panel|vp_frase_abrio_1: Possible transfer: {programa} opened 1 file{archivos} and sent {mb} to {empresa}{pais} in {min} min
p|panel|vp_defender_que: Defender has two documented settings about what it sends to Microsoft: whether it submits files as samples, and cloud protection. This is what Windows says right now.
p|panel|vp_programas_que: Antivirus and AI apps first, then the rest by volume. The company is the one of the name the program asked for; when it asked none, the owner of that address's network.
p|panel|vp_sin_programas: No measurements in this period yet.
p|panel|vp_mas_empresas: And {n} more companies with less traffic.
p|panel|vp_limites_titulo: What this view does not see
p|panel|vp_limite_contenido: The content: neither what is sent nor the files. Only sizes, moments, file names (if you turn it on) and to whom.
p|panel|vp_limite_sni: The name carried inside an encrypted connection: reading it would mean capturing packets, and GUARDIANA does not.
p|panel|vp_limite_cert: The server's certificate: with TLS 1.3 it travels encrypted. No certificate of ours is installed and nothing is decrypted.
p|panel|vp_limite_otros: The other devices at home: this is about this computer, on Windows.
p|panel|vp_limite_coste: What watching costs: Windows' network channel was already on; the file one only opens if you turn it on and lets three events through (open, read, close). It adds up every 10 seconds and is written per minute and per hour.
p|panel|cert_pagina_lead: Every month (or for the period you choose), a document made on this computer from its own chained record: which companies this computer asked for, how many times, from which countries they answered, what was blocked, and which known companies it never contacted. No IP addresses and no browsing history: by company. You keep it; GUARDIANA sends it to nobody.
p|panel|cert_campo_dominios_nota: Off, the certificate only speaks of companies. On, it adds the internet names of each known company this computer asked for; names that belong to no known company are never listed, only counted.
p|panel|cert_chip_cadena_ok: Record intact: the hash chain fully verified
p|panel|cert_chip_cadena_mal: The record's chain does not fully verify
p|panel|cert_ventana_bloqueada: The browser did not let the certificate's window open. Allow pop-ups for the panel, or use «Save .html» and open it.
p|panel|cert_falta_periodo: Choose both dates of the period.
p|panel|cert_error: The certificate could not be made:
p|panel|cert_sin_vigilar_corto: GUARDIANA was not watching for {horas} h within the period: that is not on record.
p|panel|cert_medido_distinto: The measured bytes no longer add up the same (they are pruned with the detail, or still being counted); they are not in the chain and do not change the result.
p|panel|cert_comprobar_lead: Choose a certificate .json file: GUARDIANA rebuilds it from this computer's record and tells you whether it matches. The file does not leave this computer.
p|panel|cert_estado_coincide: Rebuilt from this computer's record, it says exactly the same.
p|panel|cert_estado_mismas_filas_otra_cl: The record's rows are the same, but the figures do not match. It was made by GUARDIANA {version} (this is {ahora}), which may have assigned some names to other companies.
p|panel|cert_estado_filas_recortadas: The rows of that period have since been pruned from the record (retention period): it cannot be rebuilt; only its seal can be checked.
p|panel|cert_estado_no_coincide: It does not match this computer's record: it comes from another computer, the file was changed, or rows of the record were changed.
p|panel|cert_estado_formato_desconocido: This is not a GUARDIANA flow certificate.
p|panel|cert_estado_ilegible: The file cannot be read as a flow certificate.
p|panel|cert_subtitulo: What this computer asked the internet for from {desde} to {hasta}, according to its own chained record.
p|panel|cert_generado: Made on {fecha} (UTC) by GUARDIANA {version}, on this computer and without connecting to anyone.
p|panel|cert_extracto_nota: Extract for {empresa}: only this company is shown. The chain reference covers every row of this computer in the period.
p|panel|cert_cobertura_completa: The record covers the whole period.
p|panel|cert_cobertura_parcial: The record only starts on {fecha}: there are no rows before that (pruned by the retention period, or GUARDIANA was not there yet). Anything earlier is not certified.
p|panel|cert_cobertura_vacia: The record has no rows at all: there is nothing to certify.
p|panel|cert_sin_vigilar: GUARDIANA was not watching for {horas} h within the period ({n} stretches): whatever happened then is not on record.
p|panel|cert_empresas_ninguna: This computer did not ask for any name of a known company in the period.
p|panel|cert_sin_empresa: Names with no known company: {consultas} queries to {nombres} different names ({cortadas} blocked). They are only counted, never listed.
p|panel|cert_locales: Queries for the local network itself (printers, reverse lookups, GUARDIANA's own check), which are not destinations on the internet: {n}.
p|panel|cert_paises_t: Countries of the servers that answered
p|panel|cert_paises_lead: It is the country the database bundled in the program gives for the address that answered, not the company's: a delivery network usually answers from near you. The address is not kept.
p|panel|cert_no_t: Reference companies this computer did NOT contact
p|panel|cert_no_lead: Of the {n} companies with a checked profile in GUARDIANA ({referencia}), this computer did not ask, during the whole period, for any of the names the lists assign to them:
p|panel|cert_no_ninguna: This computer asked for names of every reference company.
p|panel|cert_medido_lead: What the Windows network channel counted per destination. These are measurements: they are sealed with this document, but the record's chain does not cover them.
p|panel|cert_medido_no: No bytes were measured in this period (they are only measured on Windows).
p|panel|cert_medido_sin_nombre: Addresses connected to without asking for a name
p|panel|cert_cadena_ok: The record's hash chain fully verified when this certificate was made: {n} rows, none altered or removed.
p|panel|cert_cadena_mal: Warning: the record's chain did NOT fully verify when this certificate was made (row {fallo}). What it says may not be reliable.
p|panel|cert_cadena_dev: This program carries the development key: it is a test build.
p|panel|cert_cadena_filas: Rows of this computer in the period: {n}. First: no. {primera}; last: no. {ultima}.
p|panel|cert_como_comprobar: How to check it: on this computer, «guardiana verify --certificado file.json» rebuilds it from the record and says whether it matches. Anywhere, «sha256sum -c file.json.sha256» checks that the .json did not change. The rows' fingerprint is the SHA-256 of their row_hash, one after another; how each row is computed is in docs/VERIFY.md.
p|panel|cert_prueba_t: What it proves and what it does not
p|panel|cert_prueba: It proves: that this computer's record was intact when it was made, and that these are the DNS queries this computer made and GUARDIANA recorded in the period, by company, country and category, with what was blocked.
p|panel|cert_no_prueba: It does not prove: what was sent or received inside those connections (GUARDIANA never reads it); whether a company holds data about you; connections to fixed addresses without asking for a name, except what the network channel measured; what happened while GUARDIANA was off or on other devices; or who was using the computer.
